candidates.name: Medulloblastoma
support_spans: a 30 × 40 × 40 mm mass lesion centered in the fourth ventricle region of the posterior fossa
causing effacement of the fourth-ventricle outlets, cerebellar compression, and tonsillar herniation
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a medulloblastoma, a common posterior fossa tumor in adults.

candidates.name: Ependymoma
support_spans: a well-demarcated, relatively homogeneous mass filling the fourth ventricle
candidates.why: The description of the mass as well-demarcated and homogeneous is consistent with ependymoma, a type of glioma that often arises in the fourth ventricle.

candidates.name: Choroid Plexus Papilloma
support_spans: a mildly hypodense mass lesion centered in the fourth ventricle region of the posterior fossa
without contrast enhancement or calcifications
candidates.why: The location and lack of contrast enhancement or calcifications are consistent with choroid plexus papilloma, a rare tumor of the choroid plexus.
